items.title: Run your whole selling business in AWS Quick
items.description: Most sellers do not need another AI product to learn. They need the tools and information they already use brought together, so they can see what is happening in their business and act on it. AWS Quick and the Amazon Selling Partner plugin do that together. Quick brings an Amazon seller’s sales data, inventory signals, and marketplace intelligence into one place, where questions become answers and answers become actions. It understands the seller’s full business context, so the seller does not need to re-explain their catalog, their margins, or their competitive landscape in every conversation. It is built on AWS, the same infrastructure Amazon uses to run its own marketplace. At Amazon Accelerate on September 23, 2026, Amazon announced the Selling Partner plugin and launched it in beta in AWS Quick. This post covers what launched, how to claim the free AWS Quick offer, and what the experience looks like day to day. It also covers how the skills and connectors work when a seller puts them to use. Limited-time offer: 12 months of AWS Quick Plus, free. Every primary selling account holder worldwide can claim a free 12-month subscription, plus access for 10 additional users you delegate. Sign up by December 31, 2026. Claim your free AWS Quick Plus offer. 1. Why Quick is right for Amazon sellers Four things make Quick a fit for how Amazon sellers already work: it learns the business, it reaches beyond the Amazon store, it turns data into decisions, and it protects seller data on infrastructure sellers already trust. Quick knows your business, not only your prompts Quick and the Selling Partner plugin connect to a seller’s inventory feeds, sales data, and operational documents. From these, Quick builds a living understanding of the catalog structure, margin thresholds, seasonality, and competitive position. Ask Quick to audit your ASINs for Q4, and it returns a ranked recommendation built on the seller’s real margin data, historical conversion, and inventory availability. Its recommendations get sharper the more the seller works with it. Quick does not stop at your Amazon store A seller’s business runs across many tools: a storefront on another channel, an email inbox, an accounting system, spreadsheets, a supplier portal. Quick connects to where the seller already works and pulls context from across the whole operation. It is a business assistant that happens to know Amazon deeply, so the seller grows overall, not on one channel alone. It turns data into decisions you can act on Sellers are not short on data. They have Brand Analytics, Search Query Performance, advertising reports, inventory health, and listing quality data. The problem is turning those signals into one clear action. Quick does the synthesis. It watches for change, flags what matters, builds the analysis, and presents the decision with the evidence behind it. Your data stays protected on the infrastructure you already sell on Quick runs on AWS and does not use seller data to train models, not for general improvement and not for anything else. Seller data stays in the seller’s environment and never informs anyone else’s models. For a seller already operating on the Amazon marketplace, there is no new security posture to evaluate. The infrastructure is the same one protecting the seller account today, and the seller’s chosen AWS Region governs where data stays. The Amazon Selling Partner plugin The Selling Partner plugin connects AWS Quick directly to live Seller Central data. After one sign-in with a Seller Central account, the plugin gives conversational access to product listings, inventory, and sales data, pulled live rather than exported and reassembled by hand. It installs like an app, with no coding required. It ships with curated Amazon skills, and it pairs with Amazon Ads MCP so campaign performance and spend sit next to the selling data. The plugin is in beta for US stores. Figure 1: The Selling Partner plugin consent screen, where the seller grants None, View, or Edit access per data category The permission screen is worth a pause. The seller grants access per data category, choosing None, View, or Edit for each, and reviews an agreement before authorizing. Nothing is all-or-nothing, and access can be narrowed or revoked later. 2. How to redeem the Quick Plus offer Claim your free AWS Quick Plus subscription (12 months free plus 10 delegated users, by December 31, 2026). Connect the Selling Partner plugin with one sign-in to your Seller Central account. It installs like an app. Ask your first question, something you would normally build a spreadsheet for. Figure 2: Connecting the Selling Partner plugin from the AWS Quick sign-up flow 3. What the experience looks like After the plugin is connected, the work happens in a conversation. You ask in plain language, Quick pulls the relevant live data, and it comes back with an answer and a recommended next step. Instead of checking a dashboard, exporting a report, and reconciling it in a spreadsheet, you move from a question to an answer to an action in one place. You review what Quick proposes before anything is sent. Figure 3: Quick diagnosing whether a sales dip comes from traffic or conversion, using live selling data 4. Two use cases a seller can build At the Accelerate workshop we had sellers build real agents live, from a plain-language description, in a few minutes. Quick turns the description into a working agent, which the seller then refines in conversation. Use case A: Inventory Launch Prep The seller is staging a new product into Amazon and wants the lowest total landed cost. The agent reads supplier data and weighs the fulfillment options per SKU on inbound cost, storage, and speed to sellable. It walks through placement choices and returns the output the seller picks: a shipping plan, a cost comparison, or a combined packet. items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now detects latency drift, idle GPUs, and missed optimizations on your inference endpoints
items.description: Every inference endpoint is well tuned the day it goes into production. Teams choose an instance type, serving configuration, and scaling settings that suit the model and its traffic at launch. With the endpoint serving smoothly, they understandably move on to the next priority. The workload, however, rarely stays still. Traffic patterns evolve, prompts grow longer, serving engines such as vLLM ship new releases, SageMaker inference develops new optimization techniques, and new fine-tuned checkpoints change the resources your model needs. Over time, a well-tuned endpoint quietly drifts. Latency and time to first token edge upward. A configuration that was never quite ideal keeps missing available performance gains. A GPU provisioned for demand that never materialized sits idle week after week. Because nothing has failed, no alarm sounds, and the drift goes unnoticed until users feel it or the bill reflects it. Amazon SageMaker AI now monitors your generative AI inference endpoints and tells you when a change could improve performance or lower cost by using Generative AI optimized inference recommendations feature with Agentic experience in SageMaker JupyterLab . Monitoring is on by default for SageMaker AI inference endpoints using vLLM serving containers and GPU instances, with no setup required, and you can opt out of endpoints. SageMaker AI looks only at operational signals: latency, GPU utilization, and the endpoint’s serving configuration. It does not read your requests or responses. From those signals, it surfaces three kinds of findings: Latency drift: A week-over-week rise in median (p50) end-to-end latency or time to first token. Unused capacity: GPUs you pay for that sit mostly idle. Configuration gaps: A serving container that’s missing newer performance improvements or security patches, or an optimization such as speculative decoding or GPU kernel tuning that your model supports but the endpoint doesn’t use. SageMaker AI sends a finding through AWS Health, with one notification per endpoint that covers that endpoint’s findings. When a notification arrives, you can act on it in one place. It opens the SageMaker AI agentic experience in Amazon SageMaker Studio with the endpoint, and its recent traffic already filled in. From there, you run inference recommendations to benchmark your current configuration against alternatives and compare them side by side on response time, throughput, and cost per million tokens. That turns a judgment call into a decision backed by data. Benchmarks run on separate compute, and nothing changes on your endpoint until you choose to apply a result. In this post, we show how SageMaker AI monitors your endpoints and how to read the notifications it sends through AWS Health. We then show how to go from a notification to a benchmarked decision in SageMaker Studio. We walk through three example scenarios, show how to apply or dismiss a recommendation safely, and explain how to opt an endpoint out of monitoring. Solution overview SageMaker AI inference recommendations follow a four-step loop: observe, notify, recommend, and decide. Each step is designed so that you stay in control, and your production endpoint isn’t changed without your explicit action. Observe – Monitoring of latency and capacity usage is on by default for eligible endpoints. It doesn’t read your requests or responses, and it carries no additional GPU cost. Notify – When there is something worth acting on, you receive a plain language notification in AWS Health, plus email, explaining what was observed, why it matters, and a recommended next step. Recommend (opt in) – One selection opens the SageMaker AI agentic experience in SageMaker Studio, prefilled with the endpoint and its observed traffic, so you can benchmark alternatives on separate compute. Decide – Compare response time, throughput, and cost side by side. Production is not changed until you apply a result. The feature produces a few types of findings. The following table summarizes what triggers each one and what gets tested when you choose to benchmark. Finding What triggers it What a benchmark tests Latency drift Response time moves relative to the endpoint’s week-over-week trends Tensor parallelism settings and alternate instance types or sizes Underutilized GPUs GPU utilization stays well below capacity over the window Cheaper instance types and smaller sizes at observed peak traffic Speculative decoding not enabled Model and container support it, but it is off (configuration based) Current configuration compared to speculative decoding enabled Serving container The endpoint’s serving container has a newer version with a performance improvement and security patches for critical and high finding Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs). Current compared to updated container Untuned GPU kernels Kernel configuration is not tuned for the model and hardware Default compared to tuned kernels Prerequisites Monitoring itself needs no setup, it is on by default. The following prerequisites apply when you choose to act on a finding by running a benchmark and, optionally, applying a change: Access to AWS Health and the AWS User Notifications console. A SageMaker Studio domain and AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions to run inference recommendation jobs and update endpoints. Sufficient service quota for the benchmark instances you want to test. Cost note: Monitoring has no GPU cost. Benchmarks use standard SageMaker AI charges, or your machine learning (ML) reservation if you have one. items.title: Inside Amazon Connect Talent: The science of structured AI interviews
items.description: For organizations hiring hundreds or thousands of people, every interview presents the same challenge: How do you give candidates a consistent opportunity to demonstrate their skills while gathering the evidence needed to make informed hiring decisions? Structured behavioral interviews offer a research-backed approach to this challenge. They use consistent, job-related questions and clear scoring criteria to give candidates an opportunity to demonstrate their skills. Decades of research in industrial-organizational (I-O) psychology have shown that structured interviews help organizations evaluate candidates and predict job performance (Schmidt & Hunter, 1998; Sackett et al., 2022). Yet delivering structured interviews at scale requires significant time and expertise to develop competencies, create q uestions, train interviewers, and evaluate responses consistently . Amazon Connect Talent brings established hiring science to AI-led interviews at scale. Connect Talent uses structured questions, adaptive follow-ups, and evidence-based scoring to help organizations gather consistent, job-related information while giving more candidates the opportunity to demonstrate their strengths. We built Connect Talent around three core design principles and evaluated how well the service applies them through a combination of internal research and independent expert review. The findings offer a closer look at the science behind Connect Talent’s AI-le d, structured interviewing. Three core design principles 1. Build interviews around job-related evidence Connect Talent builds each interview around the competencies required for the role. The service uses job requirements and established occupational frameworks to create behaviorally anchored scorecards. Each scorecard defines specific strength and concern signals, and every interview question targets the behaviors it aims to uncover. The AI interviewer also adapts to each response. After every answer, it checks whether the candidate has provided enough evidence for the competency being assessed. When details are missing, it asks targeted follow-up questions. This approach preserves the structure of the interview while giving candidates more opportunities to explain their experience. 2. Separate interviewing from scoring Connect Talent separates the interview conversation from the evaluation. The AI interviewer gathers evidence but does not assign scores. Afterward, a separate evaluation process identifies which behaviors the candidate demonstrated and cites the supporting transcript passa ges. The service calculates each competency score from 1 to 5 using a fixed formula. When the transcript lacks sufficient evidence, Connect Talent flags the competency instead of producing a score. Hiring teams can review the evidence behind each rating, and missing evidence does not automatically count against the candidate. 3. Build fairness protections into the design Connect Talent evaluates transcribed candidate responses without using video, voice tone, or physical appearance to calculate competency scores. The service also excludes candidate identity information from scoring and evaluates each competency separately. These safeguards help focus assessments on job-related behaviors and limit the influence of unrelated information. What the research shows To understand how well the se design principles work in practice, we combined independent I-O psychology evaluations with internal research. We examined whether the service generates job-relevant interview content, identifies behavioral evidence in line with expert assessments, gathers more complete responses through follow-up questions, and distinguishes between levels of demonstrated competency. Connect Talent keeps interview questions focused on job-relevant skills The quality of a structured interview starts with the skills it measures. Candidates need questions that reflect the requirements of the role, and hiring teams need confidence that the interview assesses those skills. Amazon engaged an independent I-O psychology firm to evaluate Connect Talent’s AI-generated interview content. The firm reviewed the service’s baseline output before human editing and examined how well its competencies, questions , and rubrics aligned with job requirements. The evaluation found that Connect Talent retained critical job information in 100% of the job descriptions reviewed. Of the competencies generated, 91% were clearly traceable to the job description. The firm’s psychologists also found that 98% of interview questions targeted the intended competencies, and 94% of rubric signals clearly measured the intended competency. These findings show that Connect Talent generated job-relevant interview content that met independent expert criteria in a vast majority of cases. Hiring teams can then review, select, and edit the competencies, scorecards, and questions before using them. This human oversight gives organizations control over the interview process while helping them apply structured hiring practices at scale . Connect Talent’s candidate scoring matched independent expert decisions more than 89% of the time Relevant questions provide the foundation for a structured interview. The next challenge is evaluating the evidence candidates provide with consistency. To examine this, an independent I-O psychology firm reviewed 36 interviews assessing whether candidates demonstrated specific strengths and concerns, creating 252 rubric signals. Connect Talent evaluated the same transcripts , reviewed hundreds of rubric signals , and aligned with expert scoring decisions in 89.3% of c ases . Scoring alignment reached 97.6% when candidates provided clear evidence and 92.9% when only considering candidate concern signals, which identify behaviors that may indicate a poor fit for the intended role . items.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released
items.description: PostgreSQL 19 Released Most years PostgreSQL ships a new release in September, but this year's release came two months later thanks mainly to the flurry of issues that the PostgreSQL team needed to address as part of the ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse. This release was definitely worth the wait. My favorite new feature is this one: For applications that send reads to standbys, PostgreSQL 19 adds "read-your-writes" consistency with the new WAIT FOR LSN command. A session on a standby can use WAIT FOR LSN to wait until the standby has replayed the write-ahead log (WAL) up to a specific log sequence number (LSN) before running a query, so the application can read data it just wrote on the primary. In practice, that looks like this: UPDATE movie SET genre = 'Dramatic' WHERE genre = 'Drama'; SELECT pg_current_wal_insert_lsn(); That returns a value like 0/0306EE20 . Store that somewhere (a signed cookie would work) such that on a subsequent request your application can do: WAIT FOR LSN '0/0306EE20' WITH (TIMEOUT '0.1s'); SELECT * FROM movie WHERE genre = 'Drama'; The timeout is optional - if you provide one you'll get an error if the replica you are talking to doesn't catch up within the specified time. I first encountered this pattern in Wikipedia , which has a hand-rolled version of this built against MySQL replication: In addition to this, MediaWiki attempts to ensure that the user sees events occurring on the wiki in chronological order. A few seconds of lag can be tolerated, as long as the user sees a consistent picture from subsequent requests. This is done by saving the primary binlog position in the session, and then at the start of each request, waiting for the replica to catch up to that position before doing any reads from it. Here's the relevant MediaWiki code , which these days uses MySQL's WAIT_FOR_EXECUTED_GTID_SET() function and falls back to SOURCE_POS_WAIT() . Via Lobste.rs Tags: mysql , postgresql , replication , scaling , wikipedia , ai-security-research

They recognized the Doritos bag and cancelled the alert, which notified not only other school officials on the chain, but also the Baltimore County Police Department, that no response was needed. items.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness adds Strands harness defaults, built-in tools, and lifecycle hooks
items.description: When building an AI agent, selecting a model is only the first step. The agent still needs tools, instructions for finishing the job, a way to manage context growth in long sessions, and guardrails before it executes any consequential actions, like issuing a refund. We are upgrading Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness to use Strands harness, our open-source agent harness, released earlier this year, available under an Apache 2.0 license. AgentCore harness also introduces lifecycle hooks, so you can apply your own deterministic checks and notifications at defined points in the agent loop. With this upgrade, agents that rely on the managed defaults get a recommended model, a task-oriented system prompt, automatic prompt caching (initially for Anthropic models on Amazon Bedrock), and proactive context management. They also get additional built-in tools for planning, web retrieval, filesystem access, context offloading, and task delegation. This gives agents greater capabilities during long tasks, allowing them to keep track of subtasks, reduce context window usage, and delegate work. With hooks, you can transform non-deterministic AI behavior into predictable, safe, and governed workflows by running deterministic code at specific lifecycle checkpoints. There’s no new resource type or integration to adopt. You automatically get both updates in the AgentCore harness you already use. Strands capabilities, on AWS Strands harness provides an assembled agent foundation with recommended instructions, tools, and context management. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness operates that foundation as a managed AWS service. The result is a production-grade default agent that doesn’t require you to assemble and operate the harness or its infrastructure yourself. You do not need to provision compute, bundle and host the agent loop, manage session scaling, or operate tool-execution infrastructure. Each session runs in a secure, kernel-isolated microVM in AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, with managed compute, scaling, and high availability. AgentCore achieves this by connecting the harness to the services required for production agents, including session persistence, streaming responses, usage metadata, observability, AgentCore memory, Identity, Gateway, Browser, Code Interpreter, and customer-provided containers. You retain control over the model, instructions, tools, permissions, and lifecycle policies while AgentCore manages the underlying execution environment. A more capable managed harness Harness now provides a stronger experience when you use its managed defaults: A current recommended model. When you omit the model, Harness uses a recommended default model that evolves as new models are released, always keeping your harnesses up to date. Explicit harness-level and per-invocation model configurations continue to take precedence. Task-oriented instructions. The managed system prompt encourages the agent to gather relevant context, use appropriate tools, continue until the task is resolved, adapt to failures or denied actions, and verify its work before reporting completion. The default system prompt improves over time to support the latest harness behavior. Automatic prompt caching. For supported models using Converse on Amazon Bedrock, Harness caches the system prompt, tool definitions, and conversation history. Repeated calls with the same prompt and tool surface can use lower-priced cache-read tokens, reducing input processing latency and cost. Proactive context management. By default, Harness summarizes older conversation turns while retaining recent context once the context window reaches a configurable threshold. Keeping the context lean this way helps Harness run at about 34% lower token cost than other leading harnesses . Context offloading. Large tool results can be moved out of the immediate model context. The agent receives a preview and can retrieve the complete result when needed, reducing repeated context usage without losing access to the data. Planning across invocations. The todo_write tool maintains a structured task plan that can be restored in later invocations within the same session, including after conversation summarization. Focused delegation. The subagent tool delegates a self-contained task to a fresh worker and returns the result to the parent agent. The worker is internal to the invocation, not a separately managed harness resource, and shares invocation limits and your tool-call lifecycle hooks. Web retrieval. The web_fetch tool retrieves content from a specified webpage to give your harness up-to-date external context. Granular filesystem access. With separate read , write , and edit tools, you can grant only the granular filesystem capabilities an agent needs. Customer-provided Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, AgentCore Gateway (a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore), Browser, Code Interpreter, inline functions, skills, memory, and customer-provided containers continue to work through the existing harness interfaces. Recommended by default, configurable when needed Harness manages its defaults so that agents using them receive the current AgentCore recommended experience as models, instructions, context management, and built-in capabilities improve. Explicit configuration always takes precedence: Configure a model ID to keep using a specific model. Configure systemPrompt to completely replace the managed system prompt. Configure truncation to keep a specific context-management policy. List individual allowedTools selectors to maintain a fixed tool surface. When allowedTools is omitted or set to ["*"] , Harness provides the current recommended built-in tool set. Because this set can gain capabilities over time, applications with a fixed security or capability boundary should list only the tools they need. items.title: Amazon Polly launches voice cloning: A unique voice for your brand
items.description: Voice cloning in Amazon Polly is now generally available as a gated release. Give Amazon Polly a few minutes of audio recordings from a speaker who has agreed to have their voice cloned, and Amazon Polly builds your own cloned voice in that speaker’s voice. The cloned voices run on the Amazon Polly generative engine, which delivers similar naturalness and accuracy as the rest of the generative voices. Amazon Polly voice cloning launches with seven languages: English, Spanish, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, and Hindi. Each cloned voice speaks the language it was recorded in. The cloned voices are automatically encrypted and access-controlled: only you can access your cloned voices. Amazon Polly voice cloning is available in all the AWS Regions supported by the Amazon Polly generative engine, including the AWS GovCloud (US) Region. Access is already enabled for select Amazon Polly customers. Others can reach out to their AWS account team or apply for access to get access. With this new feature addition, you can build the cloning lifecycle into AWS applications. Building a cloned voice is free for Amazon Polly customers, and Amazon Polly charges for cloned voice usage on a pay-as-you-go basis, see Amazon Polly Pricing page for details. Hear it for yourself Press play: the first few seconds are a real recording of the speaker, and then their cloned voice takes over with words they never recorded. From recordings to TTS voice. A few minutes of our science lead Trevor’s source audio, and the resulting generative voice. Recorded: “Hello, I’m Trevor, from Science.” Cloned voice: “That first sentence was my real voice. This is my cloned voice, created from a few minutes of my recordings. It can read any text you give it.” Supports seven languages. Hear Jonas, one of the authors, speaking German in his recording and then in his cloned voice: Recorded: “Hallo, ich bin Jonas. Das ist meine echte Stimme.” (Hi, I’m Jonas. This is my real voice.) Cloned voice: “Und das ist meine geklonte Stimme! Gleiche Stimme, neue Worte: Diesen Satz habe ich geschrieben, aber nie aufgenommen.” (And this is my cloned voice! Same voice, new words: I wrote this sentence, but never recorded it.) Use in a variety of applications. Here’s Trevor in a new job he hasn’t had: a non-player character in a game. “Who’s that crossing my bridge? Oh, it’s you again. Same deal as last time: answer my riddle, or hand over the sandwich.” Expand your voice library with voice cloning. Hear this audio sample from AWS Chief Evangelist Jeff Barr: a real recording, then his cloned voice. Recorded: “Hi, I’m Jeff, and this is how I really sound.” Cloned voice: “And this is how my cloned voice sounds, reading a sentence I never recorded.” Hannah: a real recording, then her cloned voice on a support line. Recorded: “Hello, I’m Hannah. This is my real voice.” Cloned voice: “Thanks for calling AnyCompany. Your order 4471 9902 ships today and should arrive on Thursday between 9 AM and 1 PM. Your confirmation code is K-7-Q-2-X-9.” Joely: a real recording, then her cloned voice narrating a lesson. Recorded: “Hi, I’m Joely, and this is how I really sound.” Cloned voice: “In this module, we’ll look at how a neural network learns. First, it makes a guess. Then it measures how far off that guess was, and adjusts, a little at a time.” What you can build A consistent brand voice across channels Establish one recognizable voice and use it across your interactive voice response (IVR) system, cascaded voice agents, mobile app, in-store announcements, advertising, and connected devices. Rather than relying on a generic stock voice or re-booking a recording session each time a script changes, you can generate on-brand audio on demand, with a consistent sound in every channel. Contact centers Deliver a distinctive, on-brand voice across self-service flows, and update prompts as offers and policies change without a new studio session. You can create prompts from source text, test them before rollout, and use the same voice across greeting, routing, and notification experiences. Media and content at scale Creators, publishers, and studios can create audiobooks, courses, podcasts, game characters, and videos in multiple custom voices to enhance the listening experience, and produce subsequent chapters or updates quickly. Localization with a consistent persona Maintain a recognizable voice identity across a content library, so narration remains coherent across titles and updates. Each cloned voice speaks only the language it was recorded in. For multilingual experiences, create and review approved voices per supported language. Accessibility and personalization Offer a natural, human-sounding voice for reading experiences, assistive tools, and personalized interactions. You confirm the speaker’s consent each time you create a voice. How voice cloning works With voice cloning, you can build a custom Amazon Polly voice from recordings of a single speaker and then synthesize speech in that voice through the Amazon Polly generative engine. The voice moves through four steps, from recording the speaker to using the finished voice: Figure 1: The voice cloning lifecycle, from recording a speaker to using the finished voice A cloned voice goes through four steps: Record. You record one speaker (see the following recording tips). You can send the recordings directly in the CreateVoice request or upload them on the console. You can also store them in an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket in the AWS Region where you want the voice and point Amazon Polly to them. Create. You call CreateVoice with 1-10 recordings, the language they are spoken in, and TermsAccepted=True , your confirmation that you have the speaker’s consent. Amazon Polly returns a voice ID ( vc-… ) right away and builds the voice in the background. Wait. Creation is asynchronous and typically takes 5-10 minutes. items.title: AIマーケティングとは？種類・活用分野10選と企業事例をわかりやすく解説
items.description: ChatGPTで広告コピーを作る程度には使っているものの、部署全体のマーケティングにAIをどう組み込めば成果が出るのか、全体像を描けていない方は多いのではないでしょうか。 AIマーケティングとは、AIを使って顧客データの分析・予測からコンテンツ制作、施策の実行までを効率化・高度化するマーケティング手法です。 すでに広告運用やメール配信でAIを使い、成果を伸ばしている企業は増えています。一方で、AIの種類と得意分野を理解しないまま導入すると、課題に合わないツールを選んで予算を無駄にしやすくなります。 本記事では、予測AI・生成AI・AIエージェントの3種類と10の活用分野を軸に、企業事例と導入の手順を中心に解説します。 読み終えたときには、自社の課題に合うAIとツールを選び、社内にAIマーケティングの導入を提案できる状態になっています。ぜひ最後までご覧ください。 AIマーケティングとは AIマーケティングとは、マーケティングの調査・企画・制作・配信・分析の各工程にAIを組み込み、成果と効率を高める取り組みです。定義に加え、従来のマーケティングやMAツールとの違いを押さえると、AIに任せる範囲を判断しやすくなります。 AIマーケティングの定義 AIマーケティングとは、顧客データや市場データをAIで分析・予測し、その結果をもとに施策の立案から実行・改善までを行うマーケティング手法です。 AIを使う理由は、顧客接点がWebサイト・アプリ・SNS・メールなどに分散し、人の手で扱えるデータ量を超えているためです。購買履歴や閲覧行動といった膨大なデータから、購入しそうな顧客や響く訴求を見つける作業はAIが得意とする領域です。 たとえば、ECサイトで閲覧履歴から興味のある商品を推薦する機能や、Google広告の自動入札も AIマーケティングの一種 です。近年はChatGPTなどの生成AIが加わり、広告文や記事の制作までAIが担えるようになりました。 AIマーケティングを「データにもとづいて顧客ごとに最適な施策を打つ仕組み」と捉えると、自社のどの業務から着手すべきかを考えやすくなります。 従来のマーケティングとの違い 従来のマーケティングとの最大の違いは、 施策の判断材料が担当者の経験からデータとAIの予測に移る点 です。 従来は、担当者が過去の経験や少数のアンケート結果をもとにターゲットを決め、同じ内容を一斉に配信する方法が中心でした。AIを使うと、顧客一人ひとりの行動データから反応しやすい内容やタイミングを予測し、配信を出し分けられます。 主な違いは以下のとおりです。 比較軸 従来のマーケティング AIマーケティング 判断の根拠 担当者の経験・勘 データとAIの予測 ターゲティング 属性で大きく分ける 行動データで個人単位に分ける 配信内容 全員に同じ内容 顧客ごとに出し分ける 改善の速さ 月次の振り返りで修正 配信結果を学習して随時修正 ただし、何を目的に施策を打つかを決めるのは人の役割です。違いを理解しておくと、AIに任せる作業と人が判断する作業の線引きを社内で説明しやすくなります。 MAツールとの違い MAツールは「人が設計したルールどおりに施策を自動実行する仕組み」であり、AIマーケティングは 「データから最適な施策そのものを導き出す仕組み」 です。 MA（マーケティングオートメーション）ツールでは、「資料をダウンロードしたら3日後にメールを送る」といったシナリオを担当者が組み立てます。ルールにない状況には対応できず、シナリオの良し悪しは担当者の設計力に左右されます。 一方で、最近のMAツールの多くはAI機能を搭載しています。購入確率の高いリードを自動で判定したり、開封されやすい配信時間を予測したりする機能です。 MAツールとAIは対立するものではなく、MAツールにAIが組み込まれていく関係 だと捉えると正確です。 すでにMAツールを導入している企業は、新しいツールを探す前に、手元のツールのAI機能を使いこなすところから始められます。 AIマーケティングで使われるAIの3種類 AIマーケティングで使われるAIは、役割によって以下の3種類に分けられます。 予測AI 生成AI AIエージェント 3種類の違いを押さえておくと、自社の課題にどのAIが効くのかを判断できるようになります。 予測AI 予測AIとは、 過去のデータからパターンを学習し、顧客の将来の行動を予測するAI です。 購買履歴やWebサイトの閲覧履歴を学習し、「この顧客は来月解約しそうか」「どの商品を買いそうか」といった確率を算出します。生成AIが登場する前から使われてきたAIで、レコメンドや広告の自動入札、リードスコアリングの多くが予測AIによるものです。 得意とするのは、数値で正解を測れる業務です。購入率や解約率のように結果が明確な指標を改善したいときに力を発揮します。 ただし、 予測の精度は学習させるデータの量と質で決まります 。顧客データが部署ごとに散らばっている企業は、データの整理から着手する必要があります。 生成AI 生成AIとは、 指示に応じて文章・画像・動画などのコンテンツを新たに作り出すAI です。 ChatGPTやGeminiが代表例で、広告コピー、メール文面、ブログ記事、バナー画像などの制作に使われます。予測AIが「誰に届けるか」を判断するのに対し、生成AIは「何を届けるか」を作る役割を担います。 マーケティングでは、1つの訴求から顧客セグメント別に数十パターンのコピーを作り分けるといった使い方が広がっています。人が1本ずつ書いていた制作物を短時間で量産できる点が強みです。 一方で、事実と異なる内容を出力することがあるため、公開前に人が確認する体制が欠かせません。 予測AIで見つけたターゲットに生成AIで作った内容を届ける ように、2つを組み合わせると成果につながりやすくなります。 AIエージェント AIエージェントとは、 与えられた目標に向けて、必要な作業を自ら判断して実行するAI です。 生成AIは人が指示するたびに1つの成果物を返しますが、AIエージェントは複数の作業をつなげて進めます。たとえば「先月の広告成果をまとめて改善案を出す」と指示すると、データの取得、集計、分析、レポート作成までを一連で処理します。 マーケティング領域では、問い合わせ対応やレポート作成、広告運用の調整など、手順の決まった業務から活用が進んでいます。SalesforceやHubSpotといった主要ベンダーも、自社ツールにAIエージェント機能を組み込み始めています。 自律的に動く分、誤った判断がそのまま実行されるリスクもあります。最初は人が最終確認する範囲に限定して使うと、安全に業務の負担を減らせます。 AIマーケティングの活用分野10選 AIマーケティングの主な活用分野は以下の10個です。 【予測AI】顧客分析とセグメンテーション 【予測AI】需要予測と売上予測 【予測AI】リードスコアリング 【予測AI】レコメンドとパーソナライズ 【予測AI】広告運用の最適化 【生成AI】記事・クリエイティブの制作 【生成AI】SEO・LLMO対策 【生成AI】SNS運用 【AIエージェント】チャットボットとWeb接客 【AIエージェント】効果測定とレポーティング 自社で手間のかかっている業務と照らし合わせながら読むと、AIを使うべき分野が見えてきます。 【予測AI】顧客分析とセグメンテーション AIを使うと、 購買行動の似た顧客を自動でグループ分けし、それぞれの特徴を把握 できます。 従来のセグメンテーションは「30代・女性・首都圏」のような属性で分ける方法が中心でした。しかし、同じ属性でも購入のきっかけや頻度は人によって異なります。 AIは購入頻度、購入金額、閲覧したページ、キャンペーンへの反応などを組み合わせて分析し、「セール時だけ買う層」「新商品にすぐ反応する層」といった行動ベースのグループを見つけ出します。人が仮説を立てていなかった顧客層が見つかることもあります。 グループごとの特徴がわかれば、訴求内容や配信チャネルを変えた施策を設計でき、一斉配信より無駄打ちを減らせます。 【予測AI】需要予測と売上予測 AIは過去の販売実績に天候・曜日・イベントなどの外部データを組み合わせ、 商品の需要や売上を予測 します。 需要予測はマーケティング計画の土台です。売れる時期と量を見誤ると、販促費をかけても在庫切れで機会を逃したり、売れ残りを値引きで処分したりする事態になります。 AIを使えば、「気温が上がる週は飲料の需要が伸びる」といった複数の要因を同時に考慮した予測が可能です。担当者の経験だけでは扱いきれない変数を加味できるため、キャンペーンの時期や広告予算の配分を決める根拠になります。 予測にもとづいて販促のタイミングを決められると、在庫と広告費の両方を無駄なく使えるようになります。 【予測AI】リードスコアリング リードスコアリングとは、見込み顧客（リード）ごとに購入や商談化の可能性を点数化する手法で、 AIを使うと点数づけの基準そのものをデータから導き出せます 。 従来のスコアリングは「料金ページを見たら10点」のように担当者がルールを決めていました。ルールが実態とずれていても気づきにくく、営業部門から「スコアが高いのに商談にならない」と不満が出る原因になります。 AIは、過去に受注した顧客と失注した顧客の行動の違いを学習し、受注につながりやすい行動に高い点数をつけます。BtoBマーケティングでとくに効果が出やすい分野です。 確度の高いリードを優先して営業に渡せるため、マーケティング部門と営業部門の連携がスムーズになります。 【予測AI】レコメンドとパーソナライズ AIは顧客の閲覧・購買履歴から好みを予測し、 一人ひとりに合った商品や情報を表示 します。 ECサイトの「この商品を買った人はこちらも購入しています」という表示が代表例です。Webサイトのバナー、メールの掲載商品、アプリのプッシュ通知なども、顧客ごとに出し分けられます。 内容だけでなく、届けるタイミングの予測にも使われます。消耗品であれば、購入日と使用量から使い切る時期を推定し、買い替えの直前に案内を送るといった施策が可能です。 顧客にとって関係のない情報が減るため、メールの配信停止や広告への嫌悪感を抑えながら、購入率を高められます。 【予測AI】広告運用の最適化 Web広告では、 入札額・配信先・ターゲットの調整をAIが自動で行う仕組み がすでに標準になっています。 Google広告のP-MAX（パフォーマンス マックス）キャンペーンやデマンド ジェネレーション キャンペーンは、AIがコンバージョンにつながりやすいユーザーを予測して配信します。人が手作業でキーワードごとの入札額を調整していた時代と比べ、運用の考え方が大きく変わりました。 そのぶん、担当者の役割は「AIに何を学習させるか」の設計に移っています。どの成果をコンバージョンとして計測するか、どの素材をAIに渡すかによって、AIの最適化の方向が決まるためです。 計測設計と素材の質を整えておくと、広告のAIが本来の性能を発揮し、獲得単価の改善につながります。 【生成AI】記事・クリエイティブの制作 生成AIを使うと、 広告コピー・メール文面・記事・バナー画像などの制作時間を短縮 できます。 とくに効果が大きいのは、バリエーションの量産です。1つの訴求軸から「価格重視の顧客向け」「品質重視の顧客向け」など、ターゲット別にコピーを数十パターン作るといった作業を短時間で行えます。 画像生成AIや動画生成AIの進化により、外注していたバナーや短尺動画を社内で作る企業も増えています。広告では複数の素材を配信して効果を比べるため、素材の数を増やせることが成果に直結します。 ただし、ブランドの世界観や表現のルールを守れているかは人が確認する必要があります。 初稿をAIに任せ、仕上げを人が担う 分担にすると、品質を保ったまま制作量を増やせます。 【生成AI】SEO・LLMO対策 生成AIは、 検索キーワードの調査から記事構成の作成、既存記事の改善案の作成まで 、SEOの作業全般を効率化します。 たとえば、上位記事の見出しを読み込ませて不足している論点を洗い出したり、検索意図に沿った構成案を出させたりする使い方です。タイトルやメタディスクリプションの案出しにも向いています。 近年は、ChatGPTやGoogleのAI Overviewsなど、AIが回答の中で情報源を引用する場面が増えました。AIに引用されやすい情報発信を目指すLLMO（大規模言語モデル最適化）も、マーケティングの新しい対策領域になっています。 ただし、AIが書いた文章をそのまま公開すると、独自性のない記事になりがちです。自社の知見や事例を加える工程を残すと、検索エンジンとAIの両方から評価されるコンテンツに育てられます。 【生成AI】SNS運用 SNS運用では、 投稿文の作成、投稿企画の案出し、コメントの傾向分析 に生成AIを活用できます。 SNSは投稿頻度を保つことが重要な一方、毎日ネタを考えて文章を書く負担が担当者に集中しがちです。生成AIに過去の反応のよい投稿を参考に渡すと、アカウントの口調に合わせた投稿案を複数出してくれます。 また、自社や競合に寄せられたコメントを読み込ませ、好意的な声や不満の傾向を要約させる使い方もあります。数百件のコメントを人が読む手間を省き、商品改善や次の企画のヒントを素早く得られます。 投稿作業の負担が減ると、担当者はユーザーとの交流やキャンペーン設計など、人が担うべき業務に時間を使えるようになります。 【AIエージェント】チャットボットとWeb接客 AIエージェントを使ったチャットボットは、 顧客の質問に答えるだけでなく、商品の提案や予約手続きまで 対応します。 従来のチャットボットは、あらかじめ登録したQ&Aの範囲でしか答えられませんでした。生成AIを組み込んだAIエージェントは、商品情報やFAQを参照しながら自然な文章で回答し、会話の流れから顧客に合う商品を案内します。 24時間対応できるため、営業時間外に訪れた見込み顧客を取りこぼしません。会話の内容は顧客ニーズのデータとして蓄積され、商品開発やFAQの改善にも活用

items.title: Optimize AI economics on Amazon Bedrock with Accenture’s sequenced approach
items.description: As enterprises scale AI on Amazon Bedrock , token spend often grows even as per-token prices fall. Without cost allocation tags in place, your cloud invoice shows AI spend as a single line item rather than by team, workload, agent, or model. Cheaper tokens expand adoption, and agentic workloads multiply invocations. As successful AI use cases scale, consumption can rise faster than unit prices drop. The economic question is whether the business value generated grows faster than the cost of the intelligence required to produce it. The Linux Foundation has launched the Tokenomics Foundation to develop open standards for AI cost economics, a sign that managing the economics of AI is now an industry discipline. In this post, you will learn about six levers for optimizing token spend, how Accenture applied them in production, and how to apply them using Amazon Bedrock. Accenture applied these levers in four client engagements across telecom, insurance, mining, and a large enterprise deployment. The same levers are available natively on Amazon Bedrock as described in this post. Where savings were measured, token spend fell by about 40–85 percent. Results are specific to each client’s workload and may vary. Client names are withheld by Accenture to protect client confidentiality. Attribution first: Measuring cost at the business level Before you optimize anything, you need to see where consumption is occurring, who owns it, and what business value it produces. Cost allocation tags at the team, workload, and agent level are the prerequisite for connecting consumption to accountable owners and, ultimately, to business outcomes. You apply them through Amazon Bedrock application inference profiles , one profile per application or workload, tagged by team, cost center, and environment. After you activate them as cost allocation tags in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console , you can use these tags to trace which teams, applications, and agents are driving spend. They also make it possible to measure the impact of each change you introduce. Three AWS services provide the underlying telemetry. AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR 2.0), delivered through AWS Data Exports , handle financial attribution, breaking down billed inference cost by workload and team after your cost allocation tags are active. Amazon CloudWatch captures operational signals such as invocation counts and latency. Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging records request-level detail, including the model used and the input and output token counts for each call. Telemetry alone isn’t enough. Engineers can read cost per invocation on a dashboard, but product owners and program leaders need a metric expressed in business terms. Accenture’s Cost per Business Transaction (CpBT) framework bridges this gap. CpBT aggregates all the model invocations, retries, tool calls, and agent handoffs that contribute to one successful business output into a single fully loaded cost figure. It surfaces the true cost of producing a result, including the failed attempts that raw token pricing hides. Tracked against the business value each workflow delivers, CpBT distinguishes a growing bill that reflects scaling success from one that reflects waste. The six optimization levers The goal of these six levers isn’t to minimize tokens at all costs. It’s to use the right amount and level of intelligence to deliver each business outcome at the appropriate cost, quality, and risk. The levers are organized into three phases based on the complexity of the change and the investment it requires. AWS and Accenture recommend working through the phases in order, and you can apply each phase independently to the workloads where it will have the most impact. Phase 1: Configuration only, no infrastructure change With Amazon Bedrock prompt caching , the model reuses the parts of a prompt that repeat across requests, such as system instructions, tool definitions, and reference documents, so you stop paying full price to process the same content again. Amazon Bedrock stores the key-value state of previously computed prompt prefixes and is designed to skip recomputation on later requests. This is designed to reduce cached input token costs by up to 90 percent for supported models (see Amazon Bedrock Prompt Caching ). Amazon Bedrock batch inference processes non-urgent workloads asynchronously as a group at 50 percent lower cost than on-demand pricing for select models (see Amazon Bedrock Pricing ). You submit inference requests as a batch job, and results are written to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) when processing completes. Batch inference suits nightly reports, document processing pipelines, and evaluation runs that don’t need an immediate response. Both levers add configuration to your existing setup. Prompt caching requires cache checkpoint markers in your prompts, and batch inference requires submitting eligible requests as a batch job instead of calling the on-demand API. Apply caching to interactive, on-demand traffic and batch inference to asynchronous work. Neither requires new infrastructure or architecture changes. Phase 2: Architectural changes Amazon Bedrock intelligent prompt routing directs requests across models within the same family, matching each task to the level of intelligence its business value, complexity, and risk require, rather than defaulting every request to the most powerful model. Intelligent prompt routing can reduce costs by up to 30 percent without compromising accuracy ( see Amazon Bedrock intelligent prompt routing ). Check Amazon Bedrock Pricing for any routing charges. In the following engagements, Accenture’s model tiering and triage routing apply this same routing lever. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) optimization tunes the retrieval step in the RAG process so that fewer unnecessary context tokens reach the model. items.title: AI人事とは？採用・評価・労務で任せてよい業務と導入時の注意点
items.description: AI人事とは、採用・評価・労務などの人事業務にAIを取り入れ、文書作成やデータ分析を任せることで、担当者が人にしかできない判断に集中できる状態をつくる取り組みです。 「経営層から人事でもAIを使えと言われたが、採用や評価に使って問題にならないか不安」と感じ、最初の一歩を決めきれない担当者は少なくありません。 AIは、誤りを人が拾える業務から始め、処遇の確定は人が担うと線引きすれば、安全に工数を減らせます。手作業の人事を続けている間に、他社は採用や労務の対応速度で差をつけていくでしょう。 本記事では、人事業務を「すぐ任せてよい業務」「条件付きで使う業務」「人が最終判断すべき業務」の3段階に分ける線引きを中心に、国内の事例と法規制への備えを解説します。 読み終えるころには、自社で最初にAIを入れる業務を決め、上長に説明できる導入案を描けるようになります。まずはAIの種類ごとの違いから確認していきましょう。 AIを人事業務に活用するとは？生成AI・予測AI・AIエージェントの違い 人事業務へのAI活用とは、 文書作成・データ分析・定型処理をAIに任せ、担当者が判断に集中できる状態をつくること です。人事で使われるAIは、得意分野によって以下の3種類に分かれます。 生成AI：文書作成と要約に強い 予測AI：データ分析とマッチングに強い AIエージェント：複数工程の自動実行に強い 種類 得意なこと 向いている人事業務 生成AI 文章の作成・要約・言い換え 求人票の作成・面談記録の要約・評価コメントの下書き 予測AI 過去データからの傾向分析 離職予兆の検知・配置候補の提案・応募者の一次整理 AIエージェント 複数の工程の連続実行 応募受付から日程調整・通知までの一連の処理 種類ごとの違いを押さえておくと、自社の課題に合うツールを選び間違えずに済みます。 生成AI：文書作成と要約に強い 生成AIは、 人事で最も導入しやすいAI です。ChatGPTやMicrosoft Copilotのように、指示文を入力するだけで文章を作れるため、専門知識がなくても使い始められます。 人事業務には、求人票、社内通知、評価コメント、面談記録など、文章を書く仕事が多くあります。生成AIに下書きを任せれば、担当者は内容の確認と修正に時間を使えます。 ただし、生成AIは 事実と異なる内容をもっともらしく出力することがある ため、人による確認が欠かせません。就業規則の解釈など正確さが求められる文書では、とくに注意が必要です。 確認する前提で使えば、文書作成の負担が大きい採用や評価の繁忙期にも余裕を持って対応できます。 予測AI：データ分析とマッチングに強い 予測AIは、 過去の人事データから傾向を学び、将来の可能性を推定するAI です。離職の兆し、成果を上げる社員の特徴、部署との相性などを数値で示します。 人の経験や勘では、数百人から数千人分のデータを同時に比べられません。予測AIは、勤怠・評価・サーベイの結果を組み合わせて分析し、担当者が見落としがちな変化を拾えます。 タレントマネジメントシステムや採用管理システムに、分析機能として組み込まれている例が多くあります。精度は学習に使うデータの量と質で決まるため、データが少ない段階では結果を参考程度に扱いましょう。 使いこなせれば、離職や人員不足が表面化する前に手を打てるようになります。 AIエージェント：複数工程の自動実行に強い AIエージェントは、 目的を与えると複数の工程を自ら判断して続けて実行するAI です。生成AIが1回の指示に1回答える仕組みなのに対し、AIエージェントは作業の流れ全体を担います。 たとえば採用では、応募書類の要約、面接日程の候補提示、候補者への連絡、カレンダー登録までを一連の作業として処理できます。担当者は、途中の確認と最終判断だけを担えば済みます。 ただし、自由度が高い分、どのシステムにどこまで操作を許すかという権限設計が欠かせません。候補者への送信前に人が承認するなど、確認の手順を工程に組み込みましょう。 権限と承認の設計を固めておけば、採用の繁忙期でも対応の遅れによる候補者の離脱を防げます。 AIを人事で活用できる業務領域5つ AIを人事で活用できる業務領域は以下の5つです。 採用：求人票作成・スクリーニング・日程調整 評価：目標添削・評価コメントの整理 育成：研修の個別提案・スキル可視化 配置・定着：最適配置・離職予兆の分析 労務：社内問い合わせ対応・勤怠データ分析 自社で工数が膨らんでいる領域と照らし合わせながら読み進めてください。 採用：求人票作成・スクリーニング・日程調整 採用は、 人事のなかで最もAI活用が進んでいる領域 です。経団連が会員企業75社に行った調査でも、人事部門のAI利用先として採用が25社と最多でした。 同調査では、採用での使い道として応募者のスクリーニングが15社、面接のサポートが13社と報告されています。求人票や採用広報文の作成、面接日程の自動調整も広く使われています。 参考： 経団連タイムス（日本経済団体連合会） ただし、 応募者のスクリーニングは合否に直結する ため、使い方に条件が必要です。詳しくは後述する「AIに任せる業務と人が判断する業務の線引き」で解説します。 文書作成や日程調整から任せるだけでも、候補者への返信が早まり、選考辞退の防止につながります。 評価：目標添削・評価コメントの整理 評価では、 AIが評価者を支える役割 を担います。評価そのものを決めるのではなく、目標設定や評価コメントの質を整える使い方が中心です。 評価の時期は、管理職が部下全員分の目標と評価コメントを短期間で仕上げる必要があります。AIに下書きや添削を任せると、記述の抜け漏れや表現のばらつきを減らせます。 具体的には、以下の使い方があります。 目標設定文が具体的で測定できる内容になっているかを確認する 評価者が書いたメモから評価コメントの下書きを作る 評価者ごとの点数の甘さ・厳しさの偏りを集計して可視化する 評価者の負担が減ると、部下との面談に時間をかけられ、評価への納得感を高められます。 育成：研修の個別提案・スキル可視化 育成では、 社員一人ひとりに合った学習を提案する用途 でAIが使われています。前述の経団連の調査では、人材育成でのAI利用が20社あり、面談のサポートが14社、研修・学習のレコメンドが11社でした。 参考： 経団連タイムス（日本経済団体連合会） 全社一律の研修では、すでに身についている内容を受講させたり、必要な人に届かなかったりする無駄が生まれます。AIは受講履歴やスキル診断の結果から、個人ごとに次に学ぶべき内容を絞り込みます。 社員のスキルを一覧にしたスキルマップを自動で更新できるため、部署ごとに不足している能力も把握しやすくなります。 リスキリング施策の対象者や優先度をデータで決められるため、研修予算の使い道を経営層に説明しやすくなります。 配置・定着：最適配置・離職予兆の分析 配置・定着では、 予測AIで配置候補や離職の兆しを見つける使い方 が広がっています。経験・適性・本人の希望を組み合わせ、異動先の候補を提示します。 離職の兆しは、勤怠の乱れやサーベイの回答の変化に表れることがあります。AIがこうした変化を早く拾えれば、上司や人事が面談などの手を打つ時間を確保できます。 ただし、 配置や離職予測の結果は、本人の処遇や評価に影響しやすい 点に注意が必要です。AIが示すのはあくまで候補や可能性であり、決定は本人との対話を経て人が行いましょう。 判断の材料として使い分ければ、優秀な社員の流出を防ぎ、適材適所の配置に近づけます。 労務：社内問い合わせ対応・勤怠データ分析 労務は、 最初にAIを導入する領域として最も向いています 。経団連の調査では、労務管理でAIを使う22社のうち19社が、労務相談の一次対応に活用していました。 参考： 経団連タイムス（日本経済団体連合会） 休暇の取り方や各種手続きなど、社員からの問い合わせは似た内容が繰り返されます。就業規則や社内FAQを学習させたAIチャットボットが一次回答を担えば、担当者は個別の相談に集中できます。 回答に誤りがあっても、社員の再確認や人事への引き継ぎで修正しやすい点も導入しやすい理由です。勤怠データから長時間労働の兆候を検知する使い方も、労務リスクの早期発見に役立ちます。 小さく始めて成果を示しやすいため、ほかの領域へAI活用を広げる際の社内説得の材料になります。 AI人事でAIに任せる業務と人が判断する業務の線引き AI人事では、 「本人の処遇に影響するか」と「誤りを人が拾えるか」の2軸 で業務を以下の3段階に分けます。 すぐ任せてよい業務 条件付きで使う業務 人が最終判断すべき業務 段階 判断の基準 主な業務 すぐ任せてよい業務 処遇に直接影響せず、出力を人が確認できる ・求人票の下書き ・面談記録の要約 ・労務問い合わせの一次対応 ・面接日程の調整 条件付きで使う業務 処遇に間接的に影響し、偏りの管理が必要 ・応募者のスクリーニング ・配置候補の提案 ・離職予兆の分析 人が最終判断すべき業務 本人の処遇を確定させる ・採用の合否 ・評価の確定 ・昇格・降格・異動の決定 自社の業務をこの表に当てはめると、AIを入れる順番と必要なルールが見えてきます。 すぐ任せてよい業務 すぐ任せてよいのは、 出力を人が確認でき、誤っても本人の処遇に直接影響しない業務 です。 求人票の下書きは担当者が読んでから公開します。面談記録の要約も、面談した本人が内容を確認できます。誤りがあっても、外部に出る前や処遇が決まる前に修正できる点が共通しています。 労務問い合わせの一次対応や面接日程の調整も、この段階に入ります。チャットボットが答えられない質問は人事担当者に引き継ぐ流れを用意しておけば、社員が困る場面を減らせます。 この段階の業務で成果を積み上げると、AI活用への社内の不安が和らぎ、次の段階に進む合意を得やすくなります。 条件付きで使う業務 応募者のスクリーニング、配置候補の提案、離職予兆の分析は、 条件を守れる場合に限って使う業務 です。 これらの業務は、AIの出力がそのまま本人の機会を左右しかねません。過去のデータに偏りがあれば、AIもその偏りを再現します。そのため、以下の3つの条件を運用に組み込みましょう。 性別や年齢などの属性をAIへの入力から外す 属性ごとの通過率などの結果を定期的に確認する 合否や処遇の確定は人が行う 3つの条件を守れない段階では、使わない判断も必要です 。条件を満たしたうえで使えば、大量の応募や社員データを公平に扱える体制を整えられます。 人が最終判断すべき業務 採用の合否、評価の確定、昇格・降格・異動の決定は、 AIの出力を参考にしても、最終判断は必ず人が行う業務 です。 処遇の決定には、本人に理由を説明する責任がともないます。「AIがそう判断した」という説明では、本人の納得は得られません。差別的な扱いが疑われた場合、会社として根拠を示せない状態にもなります。 AIの結果は判断材料の1つと位置づけ、決定者と判断理由を記録に残す運用にしましょう。後述する事例でも、AIの評価だけで合否を決めない仕組みがとられています。 判断の責任を人に残しておくと、社員からの信頼を損なわずにAIの恩恵を受けられます。 AIを人事に導入するメリット3つ AIを人事に導入するメリットは以下の3つです。 定型業務の工数を削減できる 評価や判断のばらつきを抑えられる データに基づく人材戦略を立てられる 上長に導入を提案する際の説明材料として押さえておきましょう。 定型業務の工数を削減できる 1つ目のメリットは、 繰り返し発生する定型業務の工数を減らせること です。 人事の仕事は、採用の繁忙期や評価の時期に作業が集中します。求人票の作成、日程調整、問い合わせ対応といった定型業務をAIに任せると、限られた人数でも業務の山を乗り越えやすくなります。 たとえばソフトバンクは、エントリーシートの評価にAIを取り入れた際、人事担当者の確認時間を大きく減らせる見込みを示していました。詳しくは後述する活用事例で紹介します。 空いた時間を面談や制度設計に回せるため、人事部が経営に提案する余力を持てるようになります。 評価や判断のばらつきを抑えられる 2つ目のメリットは、 評価者や面接官による判断のばらつきを抑えられること です。 人による評価は、評価者の経験や好み、その日の状況に左右されがちです。AIは同じ基準ですべての対象を処理するため、評価者ごとの甘さ・厳しさの差を見える化できます。 ただし、AIを入れれば必ず公平になるわけではありません。 学習データに偏りがあれば、AIはその偏りを引き継ぎます 。AIの結果も定期的に検証する前提で使いましょう。 基準のそろった評価は、社員が結果に納得しやすくなり、評価への不満による離職を防ぐことにもつながります。 データに基づく人材戦略を立てられる 3つ目のメリットは、 勘や経験ではなくデータを根拠に人材戦略を立てられること です。 成果を上げる社員に共通する経験やスキル、部署ごとに不足している能力をAIで分析すると、採用・育成・配置のどこに投資すべきかが明確になります。 上場企業では人的資本の情報開示が求められており、人材に関する指標をデータで説明する場面が増えています。AIで人事データを整理しておけば、開示資料の作成にも活かせます。 データで語れる人事部になれば、経営会議での発言力が増し、戦略人事への転換を進めやすくなります。 AI人事の活用事例 AI人事の活用事例として、以下の3社の取り組みを紹介します。 ソフトバンク：採用選考へのAI活用 items.title: From learning to leaderboard: How Cisco upskilled 1,200 engineers in agentic AI with AWS AI League
items.description: Cisco, like many large engineering organizations, is adopting generative and agentic AI to change how its engineers build software. The hard part is no longer access to the technology. It’s helping thousands of engineers move from watching a demo to confidently building with it. Recorded sessions and slide decks rarely close that gap. Engineers learn fastest when they build something real, see it fail, fix it, and try again. AWS designed AWS AI League for exactly that. It turns hands-on AI learning into a gamified competition, where participants customize models and build agents on AWS, get instant feedback on a live leaderboard, and compete in a game-show-style finale. Cisco is one of the clearest examples of what this looks like at scale. In 2025, Hemanth V, a Cisco software engineer, went from an internal Cisco event to being crowned the first AWS AI League Champion at AWS re:Invent 2025. In 2026, 1,200 Cisco engineers competed in an AWS AI League tournament at Cisco Transformation Fest 4.0. The winner, Nishanth Aluhonnu, earned a full event pass to AWS re:Invent 2026 in Las Vegas. In this post, we share how Cisco and AWS used Cisco Transformation Fest and AWS AI League to build a lasting culture of learning by doing. We previously covered this program in From theory to delivery: How Atos upskilled 400 engineers in agentic AI , and here we look at Cisco’s experience. We walk through Cisco’s journey, share technical lessons from the 2026 winning agent, and explain how your organization can host its own AWS AI League. What is AWS AI League? AWS AI League helps organizations build advanced AI skills through competition. Each league follows three steps: Learn – A hands-on, 2-hour workshop led by AWS experts introduces the tools and the challenge. Build – Participants experiment at their own pace and submit to a live leaderboard, with an automated evaluator giving real-time feedback after each submission. Compete – Top finalists take the stage in a live, game-show-style grand finale. Although AWS AI League offers multiple use cases, at Cisco it offered the following two challenges: Agentic AI challenge – Participants build agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore , a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale with any framework or model. The agents move through a maze-like grid, solving challenges on the way to a treasure chest. The challenges map to real-world tasks such as handling inappropriate content, running code, retrieving information from the web, and extracting structured data. Builders can choose models for supervisor and sub-agents and add tools such as AgentCore memory, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore , and AWS Lambda Event Functions . Builders use Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to apply safety controls to their agents. Model customization challenge – Participants fine-tune models in Amazon SageMaker Studio using the latest training recipes. The challenge awards points when an automated evaluator rates a participant’s customized model as more accurate and comprehensive than a reference model on the specific tasks in the competition. Finalists are scored on time efficiency, accuracy, agent planning, and token consumption efficiency. Figure 1: AWS AI League champion at AWS re:Invent 2025 Figure 2: 2026 AWS AI League winner at Cisco campus The Cisco and AWS partnership The AWS AI League story at Cisco grows out of a deep engineering partnership. Cisco and AWS bring together networking, cloud, security, and observability for shared customers including: Cisco SD-WAN , whose controller architecture runs on AWS and serves customers globally as a software as a service (SaaS) application. Cisco Meraki , Cisco Spaces , and Cisco’s IoT and smart buildings group. Cisco Cloud Control , a cloud-native, AI-powered application integrated with AWS services that brings together security, networking, observability, and collaboration. Cisco AI Defense , where Cisco’s security team uses Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI to embed AI governance and guardrails across the Cisco portfolio. The two companies have also published joint deployment guides and Cisco Validated Designs across networking and AWS. A recent example of co-innovation is SD-WAN fabric on demand across the AWS backbone, built to deliver the resilience and uptime customers expect. “When you see that many business units independently choosing to build their next-generation platforms natively on AWS, that’s not a vendor relationship anymore. It’s a true engineering partnership.” — Kumaril Kapoor, VP of Engineering, Cisco Cisco’s VP of Engineering Kumaril Kapoor and AWS Industries India leader Chandra Balani sit down to discuss the AWS and Cisco partnership story, from co-innovation across networking, cloud, and AI to enabling thousands of engineers through the annual Cisco AWS Transformation Fest. Cisco Transformation Fest: Enablement at scale As the partnership grew, it extended beyond technology to people. Working closely with Cisco teams in India, AWS saw a strong appetite for learning and experimenting among Cisco engineers across many business units. The question was how to scale that impact beyond the day-to-day touchpoints of the partnership. The answer was Cisco Transformation Fest, first held in 2022. The program is built on five tenets the team summarized as SCALE : Tenet What it means for Cisco engineers Share Share what you know with peers across teams. Connect Connect with engineers across business units. Adopt Adopt new skills and AWS services. Learn Learn by building, not by watching. Experiment / Engage Experiment hands-on and stay engaged with the technology and each other. Figure 3: 2026 Cisco AWS Transformation Fest 4.0 AWS AI League finalists Transformation Fest brings together several formats: AWS GameDays, AWS AI League, sessions where Cisco leaders share best practices and success stories with peers, and sessions on Amazon and AWS culture. items.title: Keep inference running through regional capacity shortfalls with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI
items.description: Serving a model from more than one AWS Region is a well-established pattern for highly available inference: when one Region runs short of GPU capacity, requests move to another. The pattern is simple to describe and hard to operate. Until now, if you served models on Amazon SageMaker AI managed endpoints, cross-Region routing was a piece you still had to build yourself. Today, we’re introducing cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI. It uses a new resource, the inference router, that gives your application one invocation path across the endpoints and inference components you already run, in one or more AWS Regions and AWS accounts. You register the destinations that serve a model, and your application invokes the router instead of a specific endpoint. The router keeps requests in its own Region while the local destination is healthy, shifts new requests to another registered destination when it isn’t, and returns traffic gradually after recovery. In this post, we explain how cross-Region inference routing decides where each request runs, walk through an example with one model in two Regions, and cover monitoring, limits, and what you pay. For a cross-account deployment that serves several models, see How Salesforce is advancing global-scale model serving with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI . When one Region runs short of capacity A SageMaker AI endpoint runs in one AWS Region and one account. When autoscaling can’t add instances of the type your endpoint needs, requests throttle and time out, even when the same model has spare capacity in another Region. To use that capacity, your application must detect a struggling endpoint and switch Regions, decide which errors are safe to retry without running the model twice, move traffic back after recovery without flapping, and manage access to endpoints in other accounts. That code sits on the critical path of every request, and every team serving models across Regions maintains its own version of it. How cross-Region inference routing works Cross-Region inference routing is based on a few core ideas: You decide where your model might run – For each model, you choose which endpoints and inference components the router might use. SageMaker AI decides which destination serves each request – The router prefers its own Region and shifts new requests to another destination only when the local one can’t serve reliably. Your endpoints stay the same – You deploy endpoints as you do today, with the same models, configurations, instance pools, and autoscaling. Direct InvokeEndpoint calls keep working, and the router passes InferenceId and CustomAttributes through, as InvokeEndpoint does. You can see every decision – Each real-time response tells you which destination served the request and why. A few terms describe the pieces: Inference router – A Regional SageMaker AI resource in your account that your application invokes. Routing target – A name for one logical model on a router, such as fraud-model . A router can hold many routing targets, and each fails over independently of the others. Destination – A real-time endpoint, inference component, or asynchronous endpoint registered under a routing target, identified by its full Amazon Resource Name (ARN), which tells the router its Region and account. A routing target holds either real-time destinations, which can mix endpoints and inference components across Regions and accounts, or asynchronous endpoints only. Local destination – A destination in the router’s Region, preferred while it’s healthy. Routing reason – A value returned with each real-time response that explains where the request went and why. The Region you create the router in is its local Region. To prefer a different Region, create a router there. The router doesn’t create capacity, scale your endpoints, deploy models, or copy model artifacts and container images. Each destination must already be running in its Region. Figure 1: Each request goes to a healthy destination, with the router preferring destinations in its own Region How routing decisions are made The router considers only destinations that are registered on the routing target and that it’s authorized to invoke. Among those, it prefers destinations in its own Region, and when more than one local destination is healthy, it spreads requests across them evenly. Requests leave the Region only when local destinations can’t serve reliably. To detect that, SageMaker AI calculates a health score for each destination from its recent requests, measured in the destination’s own Region. Server errors (5xx), throttles, and timeouts lower the score. Errors from the SageMaker AI platform (for example, failed health check) lower it the most. Errors caused by the request itself, such as invalid input, don’t lower it, because the same request would fail in any Region. Model latency isn’t an input, so an endpoint that keeps returning successful responses keeps its traffic. Signals such as failed instance launches or an endpoint running fewer instances than its autoscaling target make the router react faster, but only after the destination starts failing requests. The router evaluates each destination’s health and publishes it to Amazon CloudWatch as one of three states. A healthy destination serves normally. An overloaded destination still serves, and the router moves part of its traffic away. A degraded destination is failing or can’t serve, so the router moves most of its traffic away and keeps a small share to detect recovery. Figure 2: How each destination health state changes the traffic the router sends to it SageMaker AI manages failover thresholds and timing, so you don’t need to tune any thresholds. If health information for remote destinations goes stale, the router keeps traffic in its own Region, so a gap in monitoring never moves traffic on its own. items.title: Protect agent tool calls with Skyflow and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
items.description: In this post, we show how Skyflow and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway keep sensitive data out of the tools your AI agents call, and out of the model context those tools feed. We add Skyflow Detect to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway as a request and response interceptor . The Skyflow interceptor de-identifies data before it reaches a tool, restores it before the agent reads the result, and replaces documents with clean copies before the agent opens them. Your agents and tools don’t change. Skyflow is available in AWS Marketplace, and the interceptor is open source on GitHub. Agents act through tools, and tools move data Agents have moved from answering questions to taking action, and they take action through tools: Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, SaaS APIs, document stores, and web search. Every agent tool call is a data flow. Most enterprise controls cover what goes into and comes out of the model. Far fewer cover what an agent sends to its tools or what those tools send back. That gap shows up in three ways: Sensitive data leaves through tool arguments. The model writes the arguments from everything in its context, including details the tool doesn’t need. Ask an agent about a customer, and the customer’s name, account number, or email goes straight into a query to a third-party server. That server sits outside your AWS account and your compliance scope. Sensitive data comes back in tool results. Scraped web pages, CRM records, and case notes land in the model’s context, memory, traces, and logs. This happens even when the task never needed them. Documents bypass text inspection. Document tools such as Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), Box, and Google Drive return a signed URL, not text. A filter that inspects strings sees a link and lets it through, and the agent then opens the original file. Patching each agent doesn’t scale across teams and frameworks, and it can’t reach third-party tools. The controls need to sit where every tool call passes, so authorization, content safety, and data protection apply the same way to every agent and tool. AgentCore Gateway is that place. It fronts every tool an agent uses, whatever framework or model the agent runs on. It does more than route that traffic. With AgentCore Gateway interceptors, you can run your own code, as an AWS Lambda function, on every call that passes through it. A request interceptor sees each call before it reaches a tool, and a response interceptor sees each result before it reaches the agent. Either one can inspect the payload, rewrite it, or block the call. That makes the gateway a natural place to add data protection alongside Policy and Guardrails. This single control, attached once, covers every agent and every tool behind the gateway, without any change to agent or tool code. Example: A dispute-resolution agent at a large European bank Consider a large European bank with retail and corporate banking operations and strict data-residency obligations. Its operations teams are adopting agents to investigate card disputes. An analyst asks the agent to look into a disputed transaction. The agent searches the web for the merchant, then pulls the dispute case note from Amazon S3 to summarize it. Without protection, three things happen: The model builds the search query from everything in context. The search provider receives ‘Mateo Jackson dispute AnyCompany Electronics London’. That’s the customer’s name, sent to a third party, for a search that only needed the merchant. Scraped merchant pages bring unrelated personal data into the model’s context. The agent reads the original case note, with the customer’s full name, email, phone number, and card details. With the Skyflow interceptor on the gateway, the same workflow plays out differently: The search provider receives ‘[NAME_AJbrIud] dispute AnyCompany Electronics London’, where [NAME_AJbrIud] is a reversible vault token. The merchant results come back the same, the provider never learns who the customer is, and the analyst still sees the real name in the agent’s answer. Web content reaches the model already de-identified. The agent only ever receives a link to a de-identified copy of the case note. Solution overview The Skyflow interceptor is a single AWS Lambda function attached to both of the AgentCore Gateway interception points: REQUEST runs before the gateway calls a tool. RESPONSE runs after the tool answers and before the agent sees the result. At each point, it calls Skyflow Detect to find sensitive entities such as names, email addresses, phone numbers, government IDs, card numbers, dates of birth, and locations. It replaces them with tokens, or restores the originals. Skyflow Vault stores the original values so authorized systems can reverse the tokens. The Skyflow gateway configuration decides, for each tool, which of three protection modes applies: Shield the tool, Shield the model, and Shield the document. Mode What happens Who sees real data How it works Typical use Shield the tool Sensitive values are stripped from arguments on the way out and restored in results on the way back The agent and user, not the tool Uses reversible vault tokens, so values the tool echoes back are restored before the agent reads them Web search, enrichment, and third-party APIs that don’t need customer identity to do their job Shield the model Prompts, history, files and tool results are de-identified before the model reads them. The answer is re-identified on the way back Agent and user, not the model Model calls go through the gateway’s inference endpoint. On the way back, only the tokens minted for that call are restored Customer conversations, scraped web content, cross-Region or third-party models Shield the document The file’s signed URL is swapped for one pointing to a de-identified copy No one on the agent side Skyflow Detect v2 (preview) fetches the file, cleans it and stores the copy in an approved Region. items.title: PolyAI Dialog-RSN-1 is now on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
items.description: Dialog-RSN-1, a reasoning model built for real-time complex dialog, is available today on AWS Marketplace and Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. It powers frontier dialog: agents that hear a live call, reason about it, and act in real time. As an AWS customer, you can subscribe to Dialog-RSN-1 through AWS Marketplace and deploy it as a SageMaker endpoint inside your own AWS environment. You can also deploy directly from Amazon SageMaker Studio following the steps in Deploy and evaluate models with Amazon SageMaker JumpStart . That means the model designed to handle your customer conversations can be deployed like other Amazon SageMaker models with an AWS Marketplace subscription. Deploying Dialog-RSN-1 inside AWS Dialog-RSN-1 is the first PolyAI model available through AWS Marketplace . It runs inside your own AWS environment on the same AWS cloud that powers PolyAI’s compute and model training and serving. All in a single pass, Dialog-RSN-1 perceives a caller’s audio directly, reasons about what they need, and responds in real time. On SageMaker, it deploys as an endpoint like other models you run there. It is reachable from your own architecture, billed through your AWS account, and covered by the same virtual private cloud (VPC), AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles, and monitoring you already have in place. You keep ownership of orchestration, telephony integration, and business logic. Dialog-RSN-1 takes off your plate the hardest part to build yourself: understanding a live call and responding to it in real time. The endpoint speaks the OpenAI Realtime protocol, so an existing Realtime client connects through PolyAI’s bridge by changing its base URL. Audio in is 16-bit PCM mono at 16 or 24 kHz (transcode G.711 or Opus first). Connections last up to 30 minutes, and the model is English-only today. To get started, find Dialog-RSN-1 on AWS Marketplace , then deploy it straight into an Amazon SageMaker endpoint in your own account. Or you can deploy directly from Amazon SageMaker JumpStart . With Dialog-RSN-1 now onboarded to SageMaker JumpStart, deploying Dialog-RSN-1 takes one click. From the Amazon SageMaker AI console, open the Model Hub, select Dialog-RSN-1 from the JumpStart catalog, and choose Deploy. SageMaker JumpStart then spins up a real-time inference endpoint on a serving stack it has already tuned for you. No containers to wrangle, no instance types to second-guess, and no manual benchmarking. For automated workflows, the same one-click deployment also runs in a few lines of the SageMaker Python SDK. The Dialog-RSN-1 endpoint runs entirely within your own AWS account. It is deployed in your VPC, accessed through your IAM roles, and monitored with the same Amazon CloudWatch logging and metrics you use for every other workload. Because inference happens inside your account, your callers’ audio and transcripts stay within a boundary you control. For a model handling live customer conversation, this helps support your data residency and auditability requirements. Built for speed and accuracy Models built for live calls may make you choose between speed and understanding. And models built for speed may miss the meaning, and ones built for reasoning may lead to wait time for callers. Dialog-RSN-1 avoids the tradeoff. With PolyAI, you can build dialog agents that hear and handle calls the way your human agents would. These agents catch hesitation, hear frustration before it escalates, and know when to speak. Real-time customer conversation is the job PolyAI’s Dialog-RSN-1 is built for, and it is already handling live calls in production today. Because the model reasons directly over the caller’s audio, it picks up tone, hesitation, and timing, the signals a plain transcript loses, and decides for itself the right moment to respond. A model that hears calls the way humans do Dialog-RSN-1 is a model focused on real-time conversations. There is no separate speech-to-text step and no reasoning model on the appropriate moment to talk, so thereby no multiple handoffs. In practice, that means the callers get responses faster: Barge-in keeps working even when call volume spikes, instead of getting switched off to protect performance. Responses keep pace, so the model is not lagging behind the conversation while it reasons through what to say. Transcription is produced from the audio itself, because Dialog-RSN-1 is reading the actual audio, not someone else’s best guess at it. Dialog-RSN-1 on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart Amazon SageMaker JumpStart is the machine learning hub inside Amazon SageMaker AI, and it exists to collapse the distance between choosing a model and running it in production. For Dialog-RSN-1, that means the frontier of real-time dialog is a few clicks away. You can discover it, prove it on your own data, and ship it to a secure endpoint, all in one place. Here is what you get. Figure 1: The Dialog-RSN-1 model card in SageMaker JumpStart The code path using the SageMaker Python SDK is explained in our GitHub repository: Deploy PolyAI Dialog-RSN-1 on Amazon SageMaker AI . Discover and evaluate before you commit Dialog-RSN-1 shows up in the SageMaker JumpStart catalog with overview and sample notebooks in one place, so your team can understand the model before spending a dollar on infrastructure. To try the model on your own calls, deploy the endpoint and run PolyAI’s sample notebook, which streams recorded caller audio and prints the model’s turn decisions, replies, and transcripts. One-click deploy and optimizations for your workload From the same model card you choose Deploy, and Amazon SageMaker JumpStart stands up a real-time inference endpoint with a pre-configured serving stack. There is no manual container selection or instance guesswork. The real convenience is the named optimization profiles: instead of hand-tuning infrastructure, you pick the target that matches how you run Dialog-RSN-1. items.title: Using NVIDIA Run:ai GPU Fractioning on Amazon EKS
items.description: GPU sharing is not new: Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), time-slicing, and Multi-Process Service (MPS) address different isolation and utilization needs. NVIDIA Run:ai GPU Fractioning builds on MPS with Kubernetes-integrated scheduling, per-Pod memory contracts, enforcement, and metrics. NVIDIA Run:ai is AI workload orchestration software for Kubernetes. Its GPU Fractioning Operator can help several teams share one or two GPUs on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) . Notebooks, model evaluations, and small inference services can leave teams waiting even when GPU memory remains available. In this walkthrough’s baseline, the NVIDIA device plugin exposes the single GPU as one nvidia.com/gpu resource, with GPU sharing disabled. Two Pods each requesting nvidia.com/gpu: 1 cannot run concurrently on that node, even when their combined GPU-memory demand fits. NVIDIA Run:ai GPU Fractioning adds Kubernetes scheduling integration, enforced GPU-memory limits, and per-Pod metrics to software-based sharing. The approach applies to NVIDIA GPUs that meet the GPU Fractioning Operator’s hardware and software requirements, including GPUs without MIG. We use one Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) g5.xlarge instance with an NVIDIA A10G Tensor Core GPU as the validated example. Other configurations require compatibility checks and validation. NVIDIA announced the open source release of NVIDIA Run:ai on October 13, 2026. This example uses two of its four modular components: KAI Scheduler and GPU Fractioning Operator . KAI Resource Management and Workload Map address organizational governance and additional workload types, outside this walkthrough’s scope. In this post, we show how to build a custom Amazon Linux 2023 (AL2023) image and configure GPU-memory sharing on Amazon EKS. In the validated G5/A10G example, you establish a whole-GPU baseline, give each Pod an 8 GiB memory contract, and verify 6 GiB allocations. You then inspect per-Pod metrics, test rejection of a 9 GiB allocation, and clean up the disposable environment. Choose a GPU sharing approach MIG provides hardware partitions on supported GPUs . Device-plugin time-slicing shares a GPU without replica memory or fault isolation. MPS permits concurrent CUDA processes. Fault containment depends on configuration. NVIDIA Run:ai GPU Fractioning adds enforced per-container memory limits and supports time-slicing (default) or sm-sharing compute modes. NVIDIA documents separate workload error domains for its default mode and a shared error domain for sm-sharing. These are not security guarantees. This walkthrough tests memory limits, not fault containment or compute performance. A memory limit does not reserve proportional compute. Amazon EKS documents several GPU sharing options: MIG , time-slicing with the NVIDIA device plugin , and time-slicing with the NVIDIA DRA driver and Karpenter . For guidance on choosing among them, see the GPU sharing guidance in the Amazon EKS Best Practices Guide. Choose GPU fractioning when you need enforced per-Pod GPU-memory limits on GPUs without MIG and can run fixed-size GPU node groups. Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) provides Kubernetes APIs for requesting and allocating devices. GPU sharing and isolation depend on the device driver’s implementation and enabled features. KAI Scheduler and GPU Operator support DRA. This walkthrough uses NvFractions annotations, not DRA. GPU fractioning can help interactive notebooks with idle periods, short evaluation jobs, GPU compatibility tests, and small inference services. Choose each GPU-memory request from measured peak usage plus overhead, then test latency under concurrent load. The demonstrated density improvement does not establish a throughput gain or a universal cost reduction. Solution overview The following diagram shows the validated single-GPU environment in the US East (Ohio) Region (us-east-2). You use the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) , eksctl, Helm , and Packer to build and operate it. The Amazon EKS control plane runs Kubernetes version 1.36 in an AWS managed Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) , separate from the customer VPC. It connects to EC2 workers in private subnets of the customer VPC. An m7i.large system node hosts the operator controllers and KAI Scheduler. KAI Scheduler places both Pods on a tainted g5.xlarge with one A10G containing 23,028 MiB of GPU memory. Each Pod has an 8 GiB GPU-memory limit and allocates 6 GiB of GPU memory. The GPU worker uses custom AL2023 with the NVIDIA R615 driver branch , NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and containerd. It runs fractiond with Node Resource Interface (NRI) integration and MPS for sharing. The metricsd daemon exports per-Pod GPU-memory metrics. Figure 1: Validated example of two GPU-memory contracts on one A10G in Amazon EKS Implementation walkthrough The walkthrough uses the AWS Samples repository. Confirm the prerequisites and validated component versions, then complete Steps 1 through 10. Prerequisites Use an AWS account with permissions for Amazon EKS, AWS CloudFormation , Amazon VPC, Amazon EC2, Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) , AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) , and AWS Systems Manager for Amazon Machine Image (AMI) discovery. Confirm quota and capacity for g5.xlarge, the system node, and a temporary m5.xlarge image builder. Install AWS CLI v2, eksctl, kubectl, Helm, Packer, Git, jq, and curl. Use your normal AWS credential provider: a named profile, AWS IAM Identity Center , an assumed role, or access-key environment variables. Prefer temporary credentials. AWS_SESSION_TOKEN is required when using temporary access keys. The examples use us-east-2. Another Region must support the selected Amazon EKS version and instance types. Before choosing another GPU, check NVIDIA’s GPU Operator hardware list , the selected driver’s hardware support , and the GPU Fractioning Operator prerequisites .
